title: Songs Jackson sang with Calloway and Bennie Payne
summary: He sang popular ballads Calloway did not want to do, took over Bennie Payne's tunes after Payne left, and remembers Payne's friendship.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: I wonder -- tell me about some of the songs you sang in that band, Brother, because you --
Oh, gee whiz, I used to sing "Out of Nowhere." I used to sing Besame Mucho. I used to sing "I
Concentrate on You." I used to sing 'As Time Goes By.'
'As Time Goes By.' Yeah, I remember that one. Tell me about the --

And the first song that I sang, oh, gee whiz, I'll have to think that over. But I enjoyed every tune. Calloway used to -- it looked like he always gave me the tunes that he didn't want to do but they had to be played because they were popular tunes, --
They were popular tunes.
That's right. -- and tunes that I guess he thought he himself wouldn't do, you know.
Well, he didn't have the in-depth musically to do some of those intricate tunes like 'I Concentrate on You.'
Yeah, I know.
That's, of course, a hard one for a singer to sing.
And 'The Night We Called It a Day?'
Yeah.
And I used to -- Well, after Payne left, you know, I got the tunes that Payne used to do, a lot of them I got to do later on, --
Right.
-- you know, like Just Worrying for You --
That's right.
-- and 'Don't Worry About Me,' you know, and those tunes like that that Payne used to do when he left, you know.
Right.
Payne showed me a lot of things, you know.
Yeah, he was a [ ] .

You know, Payne and I was kind of close, you know. Payne, he admired what I could do, you know, and Payne used to talk to me. The only time that he didn't talk to me, if he got in a blackjack game with me he wouldn't talk to me.
